conviction_note: The one line this print can turn on is the FY2026 '~100% revenue growth' target. FY2025 gross revenue was $5.2M, so the target is about $10.4M. H1 was $3.2M, which leaves about $7.2M (~$3.6M a quarter) for H2. Q3 shows only ~$1.2M of disclosed international orders plus a ~$1M domestic run-rate. So a cut or a 'timing' walk-back is more likely than a reaffirm. That lean is arithmetic from company documents, not a disclosed number, and it is shrunk for a crowded short (~17% of float, 15-19 days to cover) and for a stock already 57% off its high. Hence p_up 45 on abs 8 (-0.8 scaled) against a findings sum of -0.1. The gap exists because the positioning finding (+1.0) offsets most of the guidance negative in the sum, while in p_up I kept a mild negative lean.
bar: No sell-side consensus could be sourced: stockanalysis lists analyst count n/a, Digrin's estimates are paywalled (https://www.digrin.com/stocks/detail/WRAP/earnings), and MarketBeat (403) quoted a $1.61M Q4-2025 revenue estimate, so some thin coverage exists but it is not visible. The only sourced bar is the company's own FY2026 target of ~100% revenue growth on FY2025 gross revenue of $5.2M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1702924/000149315226012909/ex99-1.htm, 2026-03-26), i.e. ~$10.4M. Against H1 2026 revenue of $3.2M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1702924/000149315226037136/ex99-1.htm, 2026-08-11), that implies ~$7.2M for H2, ~$3.6M a quarter (the same arithmetic appears at https://finsee.ai/earnings/wrap/2026/q2/en/). print_vs_bar_pct compares my Q3 estimate of ~$2.6M with that $3.6M implied pace. It is NOT a beat/miss against a street number, so the reported-quarter finding is capped small. Q3 2025 comparison: $2.0M gross / $1.5M net.
positioning_check: Short interest is 7,654,344 shares at the 2026-10-30 settlement (7,840,611 on 10-15, 7,526,221 on 9-30), with 18.78 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/wrap/short-interest). stockanalysis puts it at 16.96% of a 45.14M float with 14.84 days to cover (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/wrap/statistics/, page updated 2026-11-16). That is a crowded short, likely partly hedges by convertible/warrant holders: the Series A/C preferred and warrants carry full-ratchet terms, and Iroquois is the named Series C holder. No usable skew: the chain is unusable, with ATM spread 153% of mid and ATM IV 364%. Put/call open-interest ratio is 0.38 on 2,370 contracts. Insider ownership is ~27% (CEO Cohen ~12.9M shares). Run-up is +5.2% over 5 days and +0.4% over 20 days; spot $1.315 is 57.6% below the 52-week high and 28.9% above the low.

findings.finding: The FY2026 '~100% revenue growth' target needs ~$7.2M of H2 revenue (~$3.6M a quarter) after H1 of $3.2M, against a Q3 with only ~$1.2M of disclosed international orders scheduled for recognition. On the Q2 release management already softened from 'continues to target' (Q1, May 13) to 'we are not updating that prior target' and 'final revenue for 2026 may differ materially'. A cut, withdrawal or 'timing slip' of the target on this print is more likely than a reaffirmation.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 print (2026-05-13): $3.2M bookings and 'continues to target ~100%... supported by trends observed throughout Q1', and the stock rose +14.58%. Q2 2026 print (2026-08-11): revenue +103% and GM 75%, but the target language softened to 'not updating', and the stock fell -7.49% (baseline). On this name the guide language has carried the reaction, not the reported quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: No visible consensus models H2, so nobody publishes the $7.2M H2 requirement against the Q3 order book. If the market had priced a cut, the stock would have fallen on the July 13 'reaffirm' and the Q2 softening and would sit at the 52-week low. Instead it is 29% above the low and +5% in five days into the print. Partly priced: the stock is 57% off its high and already fell 7.5% on the softer Q2 language.
findings.independence: The FY2025 base of $5.2M comes from a different document, the 2026-03-26 8-K ex99-1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1702924/000149315226012909/ex99-1.htm). The Q3 order disclosure of ~$1.2M Brazil/India 'scheduled for revenue recognition in the third quarter' is from the 2026-07-14 release (https://samsearch.co/government-contracting-news/wrap-technologies-secures-12-million-in-international-orders-for-bolawrap-150-140774). Finsee independently computes the $7.2M H2 implied figure (https://finsee.ai/earnings/wrap/2026/q2/en/). No sourced Q3 domestic order announcement exists for Aug-Sep 2026 (searched).

findings.finding: Q3 2026 revenue should show yoy growth but not doubling. The ~$1.2M Brazil/India BolaWrap order is booked for Q3 recognition, and on top of a domestic run-rate of roughly $1M a quarter (Q1 total $1.1M, Q2 $2.1M) that gives an estimated ~$2.2-2.8M. The comparison is Q3 2025 at $2.0M gross / $1.5M net, the strongest quarter of 2025. So the headline yoy growth will be well under the 100% pace.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue +103% yoy with GM up to 75% from 48%: the stock fell 7.49%, so a strong reported quarter was sold when the guide language softened. Q3 2025 revenue +241% gross: +1.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Without a published consensus, nothing shows where the market sits on Q3 revenue, so this is capped small. If a sequential step-up to ~$2.5M were priced against a market expecting less, the July order news would have lifted the stock durably. It did not: the stock is down from ~$1.40 at the August raise.

findings.finding: The August raise put cash at roughly $10-12M at September 30: 5,771,519 shares plus 2,800,090 pre-funded warrants at $1.40, $12.0M gross and ~$10.8M net (Maxim), on top of $4.8M at June 30, less the ~$1.7M balance of the $2.0M Frenel preferred investment closed July 8, less ~$1.2-2M quarterly operating burn. That is 4-6 quarters of runway, so a post-print discounted raise is less likely than usual for this name. The money funds WrapShield/federal commercialisation and the Frenel license.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Past raises followed prints closely (Feb 2025, Aug 2025, Feb 2026, Aug 2026, the last a week after the Q2 print). No print in the baseline window was immediately followed by a cash scare.
findings.why_not_priced: The pattern of raising right after prints is what a holder would fear into this print. Cash in hand reduces that risk, but the number becomes visible only with the 10-Q/release. The raise itself is public, so this is mostly priced and sized small.

findings.finding: The short is crowded and has been rising: 7.65M shares, ~17% of the 45.1M float, 15-19 days to cover on ~400-500k average daily volume. Any reaffirmation of the FY target or a sizeable federal/drone order disclosed on the call has a squeeze mechanism behind it.

findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is a mechanism, not a fact the price absorbs. If shorts expected a clean miss they would have pressed into the print, but SI fell slightly from 7.84M to 7.65M in the last settlement. Part of the short is likely a hedge against the convertible preferred and warrants, which caps the squeeze.

baseline_tension: There is no usable skew or option-implied move. The 20-day run-up is flat and the 5-day is +5%, so my negative guidance lean goes against a small pre-print bid and is softened by a crowded short of ~17% of float. That keeps p_up close to 50, at 45.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks a negative): guidance finding cut from -2.5 to -2.0, and p_up raised from 44 to 45.
Lesson 6 (bar unsourced at the quarterly level): reported-quarter finding capped from +0.5 to +0.4; the guidance finding stands because it is sized against the company's own FY target.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the cash/runway finding was re-signed from -0.3 to +0.3. The money funds WrapShield/Frenel, there is no going-concern flag, and the dilution overhang resolves 2026-12-11, outside the window.

Lessons 1-2: the guidance finding is kept as the main line, because this name's reaction followed guide language (+14.6% on a confident target, -7.5% on 'not updating') rather than the reported quarter.
